blocks.text: Why do architects use copper roofs in modern design

Copper is a material that rewards patience. When first installed, it has a bright metallic shine. Over decades, exposure to the elements creates a protective layer called a patina. This process is not just visual. It shields the underlying metal from environmental damage. This makes copper a top choice for projects where longevity is the primary goal.
The administrative burden of material specification

Specifying materials is often the most tedious part of the job. You must reconcile aesthetic vision with fire ratings, structural capacity, and procurement rules. Many architects default to manufacturers they already know. This happens because research takes too much time. You are likely already juggling dozens of emails per day. Adding a new material search to that list feels impossible.
Fixing the specification workflow on Mac

items: Adopt a single source of truth for all material data to prevent version conflicts.
Use automated status tracking for approvals instead of long email threads.
Engage manufacturers early to resolve technical trade offs before final specs are set.
Keep your Mac file system organized with consistent naming conventions for all spec sheets.
